questions.stem: A 32-year-old man has a 1-week history of diarrhea, bloating, and excessive gas. He describes his stools as very foul-smelling, greasy, and floating. The week before symptoms began he went on a camping trip, slept outside, and drank unfiltered stream water. He is otherwise healthy. Microscopic examination of the stool shows rapidly motile single-celled organisms that have two nuclei and flagella. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balantidium coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giardia lamblia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leishmania spp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trypanosome spp.

explanation.summary: Greasy, foul-smelling stools after drinking untreated surface water, with binucleate flagellated protozoa in stool, indicate giardiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Giardia lamblia is a flagellate protozoan whose organisms show two nuclei and flagella, exactly as described on stool microscopy. G. lamblia survives in the environment for months, so campers and people who drink unfiltered outdoor water are at risk in addition to person-to-person fecal-oral spread. Beyond generic gastrointestinal symptoms, giardiasis characteristically produces smelly, greasy, fatty stools.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Balantidium coli is a ciliate whose surface is covered by cilia rather than a few flagella, and it has no binucleate appearance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Leishmania spp. are flagellates, but they are not acquired by drinking contaminated water and do not produce fatty stools.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Naegleria fowleri is an amoeba that moves by pseudopods and causes a brain infection, not watery greasy diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trypanosome spp. are flagellates that are not transmitted in stream water and are not diagnosed by stool microscopy.

questions.stem: In everyday usage, a parasite is any organism that lives on or inside a host and takes nutrients from it. In medicine, however, the word is applied much more narrowly. Which of the following descriptions matches the medical definition of a parasite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A eukaryotic fungus that invades and damages host tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: A eukaryotic organism that infects humans and is not a fungus

choices.label: C
choices.text: A prokaryotic organism that colonizes the host intestine

choices.label: D
choices.text: An agent that is neither prokaryotic nor eukaryotic in structure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any organism that takes nutrients from the host it lives on

explanation.summary: Medically, a parasite is a eukaryotic organism that infects humans but is not a fungus.
explanation.whyCorrect: The medical definition deliberately excludes bacteria, viruses, and fungi. Bacteria are prokaryotic and therefore not classified as parasites, and viruses are neither prokaryotic nor eukaryotic, so they also fall outside the category. What remains are eukaryotic, non-fungal organisms such as protozoa and helminths.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fungi are eukaryotic but are specifically excluded by the medical definition of a parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bacteria are prokaryotic, so they are excluded from the medical definition even though they take nutrients from the host.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This describes viruses, which are neither prokaryotic nor eukaryotic and therefore fall outside the medical category.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is the broad, general definition, under which most pathogens would qualify as parasites.

questions.stem: Parasites are broken down into two broad categories, ectoparasites and endoparasites. Which of the following features defines an ectoparasite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It interacts only superficially and does not invade deeper tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is always multicellular, whereas endoparasites are single-celled

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is prokaryotic, whereas endoparasites are eukaryotic organisms

choices.label: D
choices.text: It provides a nutritional benefit to the host it colonizes

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires an arthropod vector, whereas endoparasites are ingested

explanation.summary: An ectoparasite interacts only superficially with its host and does not invade deeper tissues.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ectoparasites such as mosquitoes, ticks, fleas, lice, bedbugs, and mites live on the surface of the host. Endoparasites, by contrast, infect beyond the skin and advance into the organ systems. The superficial versus deep distinction, not size or cell type, is what separates the two groups.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Both groups contain multicellular members; helminths are multicellular endoparasites, so this does not separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither group is prokaryotic; parasites by the medical definition are eukaryotic organisms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Parasitism is a one-sided relationship in which the host receives no benefit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ectoparasites can be vectors themselves rather than requiring one, and endoparasites are acquired by many routes.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with an intensely itchy rash on his hands, feet, and waistline that is worst at night and disturbs his sleep. Physical examination shows small erythematous papules and burrow-like tracks between the fingers. He has been staying in a crowded shelter since losing his home to a natural disaster. Which of the following is the most likely etiologic agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Necator spp.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Plasmodium vivax

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sarcoptes scabiei

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: An intensely itchy papular rash with burrows between the fingers, acquired in crowded living conditions, is scabies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sarcoptes scabiei is a microscopic mite that burrows into the skin and is transmitted through close personal contact or shared fomites, which makes crowded settings such as shelters, jails, childcare facilities, and nursing homes high risk. The lesions are small papules, burrows, and excoriations that favor the finger webs, skin folds, waistline, genitals, nipples, and buttocks. Itching is characteristically worse at night.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Diphyllobothrium latum is the fish tapeworm and causes gastrointestinal symptoms after eating undercooked fish.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Necator spp. are nematodes that penetrate the skin of bare feet and then infect the gastrointestinal tract.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasmodium vivax causes malaria with cyclic fever and chills and is spread by the Anopheles mosquito.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Wuchereria bancrofti is transmitted by mosquito bites and causes lymphatic filariasis with massive limb swelling, not burrows.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has a scabies infestation with an intensely pruritic papular rash. The mites in her skin release soluble antigens in their saliva, eggs, feces, and other secretions. Which of the following best describes the immune reaction these antigens provoke and the cell chiefly responsible for the resulting tissue injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct complement activation, with the alternative pathway lysing host epidermal cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Type I hypersensitivity, begun by IgE and mast cells and then dominated by eosinophils

choices.label: C
choices.text: Type II hypersensitivity, with IgG binding antigens on host keratinocyte surfaces

choices.label: D
choices.text: Type III hypersensitivity, with immune complexes depositing in dermal blood vessels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type IV hypersensitivity, with sensitized T cells recruiting and activating macrophages

explanation.summary: Scabies antigens trigger a Type I hypersensitivity reaction that is quickly taken over by eosinophils, which cause the tissue damage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Soluble mite antigens produce a Type I hypersensitivity reaction initiated by IgE and mast cells. That initial reaction is rapidly dominated by eosinophils, which release the factors ultimately responsible for tissue injury. This mechanism explains why the rash is so intensely itchy and inflamed relative to the small number of mites present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complement-mediated lysis of host epidermal cells is not the pathway described for scabies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibody directed against antigens fixed on host cell surfaces is not how the mite antigens act here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune complex deposition in vessel walls is not the described mechanism of scabies skin injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The reaction is not a delayed, T cell and macrophage driven process; it begins with IgE and mast cells.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old nursing home resident has an itchy papular rash with excoriations over the trunk and hands, and the physician suspects scabies. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Colonoscopy with inspection of the bowel for attached worms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giemsa-stained thick blood smear examined for larval worms

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lumbar puncture with microscopic examination of spinal fluid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skin scraping examined microscopically for mites, eggs, or feces

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stool examination for cysts and flagellated organisms

explanation.summary: Scabies is confirmed by scraping the skin and identifying the mite, its eggs, or its feces under the microscope.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because Sarcoptes scabiei lives in burrows within the superficial skin, scraping the involved skin samples the organism directly. The scraping is examined under the microscope for the mite itself, its eggs, or its feces. No blood, stool, or spinal fluid testing is needed for this superficial ectoparasite.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colonoscopy detects intestinal helminths and would not sample a mite living in the skin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A Giemsa-stained thick blood smear is used to look for bloodborne worm larvae, such as in lymphatic filariasis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spinal fluid examination is used when a brain infection such as primary amebic meningoencephalitis is suspected.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stool examination for cysts and flagellated organisms is how giardiasis is diagnosed.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old infant is brought to clinic with an intensely itchy rash, and skin scraping confirms Sarcoptes scabiei. Compared with the usual pattern in healthy adults, which of the following distributions is most characteristic of scabies in infants and immunocompromised patients?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Finger webs, wrists, and waistline only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genitals, nipples, and buttocks only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Groin and axillae, with sparing of the hands

choices.label: D
choices.text: Head, face, neck, palms, and soles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lower legs at the site of larval entry

explanation.summary: Infants and immunocompromised patients with scabies may develop rash on the head, face, neck, palms, and soles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scabies lesions can appear anywhere on the body, but in healthy adults they are most commonly found between the fingers, in skin folds, along the waistline, and on the genitals, nipples, or buttocks. Infants and immunocompromised patients extend beyond that adult pattern and may have rash on the head, face, neck, palms, and soles. Recognizing this broader distribution prevents a missed diagnosis in these groups.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Finger webs, wrists, and waistline describe the classic adult pattern, which is the comparison group in this question.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genitals, nipples, and buttocks are also typical adult sites rather than the distinguishing infant pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Scabies characteristically involves the hands, so a pattern sparing them does not fit this infestation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lesions at a larval entry site on the legs describe skin-penetrating nematodes, not a burrowing mite.

questions.stem: A patient with an intensely itchy rash that is worse at night has thin, winding, snake-like lines in the skin of the finger webs in addition to small papules and excoriations. Which of the following best explains these linear lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excoriations created entirely by the patient's own scratching

choices.label: B
choices.text: Linear pustules that follow the course of cutaneous nerves

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serpiginous burrows made as the mite tunnels through the skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vesicles formed by mast cell degranulation around dermal vessels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wheals caused by adult worms moving through subcutaneous fat

explanation.summary: The snake-like lines of scabies are burrows tunneled by the mite and are described as a serpiginous rash.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scabies mites burrow into the skin, and the resulting tunnels can be seen on the surface as lines that look like snakes. These are called serpiginous rashes and are a hallmark of the infestation. They occur alongside the small papules and excoriations, and the associated itching is characteristically worse at night.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Scratching produces excoriations, but the winding tracks are made by the mite itself as it burrows.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The burrows follow the mite's path through the skin, not the distribution of cutaneous nerves.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Although mast cells participate in the hypersensitivity response, the visible lines are tunnels, not vesicles around vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No adult worm migrates through subcutaneous fat in scabies; the organism is a microscopic mite in the skin.

questions.stem: Over 6 weeks, several residents of a nursing home develop intensely itchy rashes with burrows, and two staff members become affected as well. Which of the following best explains how the responsible organism spread through this facility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bites from mosquitoes breeding in standing water nearby

choices.label: B
choices.text: Close personal contact and sharing of contaminated fomites

choices.label: C
choices.text: Drinking tap water that contains environmental cyst forms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion of food contaminated with parasite eggs and feces

choices.label: E
choices.text: Walking barefoot on soil that contains infective larvae

explanation.summary: Scabies spreads by close personal contact and shared fomites, which is why outbreaks cluster in crowded institutions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transmission of Sarcoptes scabiei occurs through close personal contact or shared fomites such as bedding and clothing. That is why outbreaks are common in childcare facilities, jails, and nursing homes, where people are in sustained close contact and share items. Staff who handle residents and their linens are exposed by the same route.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mosquito bites transmit organisms such as Plasmodium spp. and Wuchereria bancrofti, not a skin-burrowing mite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Contaminated drinking water transmits protozoa such as Giardia lamblia rather than an ectoparasitic mite.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fecal-oral ingestion transmits organisms such as Giardia lamblia and Ascaris spp., not scabies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Soil contact with bare feet transmits skin-penetrating nematodes such as Strongyloides, Ancylostoma, and Necator spp.

questions.stem: A lecturer states that, after humans, mosquitoes are the most lethal animal on earth, even though an individual mosquito bite causes only a small local reaction. Which of the following best explains this statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mosquito bites cause fatal anaphylaxis in most exposed people

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mosquito saliva contains a toxin that is lethal in large doses

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mosquitoes act as vectors for parasites, bacteria, and viruses

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mosquitoes invade deep tissue and destroy the lymphatic system

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mosquitoes reproduce within human skin and cause chronic rashes

explanation.summary: Ectoparasites such as mosquitoes are dangerous mainly because they transmit other pathogens, not because of the bite itself.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ectoparasites in and of themselves are largely an inconvenience, but their role as vectors for other parasites and microorganisms is deadly. Mosquitoes carry parasites, bacteria, and viruses, and the infections they spread cause millions of deaths worldwide every year. Malaria alone, transmitted by the Anopheles mosquito, is the most lethal parasitic infection on earth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Most bites cause only a minor local reaction rather than fatal systemic allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The danger comes from organisms the mosquito carries, not from a toxin in its saliva.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The mosquito is a superficial ectoparasite; it is the worm it can transmit that damages the lymphatic system.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mosquitoes do not reproduce inside human skin; that behavior belongs to mites such as Sarcoptes scabiei.

questions.stem: Endoparasites are further broken down into two subcategories. Which of the following correctly distinguishes those two groups?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Protozoa are always motile, whereas helminths are never motile

choices.label: B
choices.text: Protozoa are multicellular, whereas helminths are single-celled

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protozoa are prokaryotic, whereas helminths are eukaryotic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protozoa are single-celled, whereas helminths are multicellular

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protozoa infect only skin, whereas helminths infect organ systems

explanation.summary: Endoparasites are subdivided by cellularity: protozoa are single-celled and helminths are multicellular worms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both groups are endoparasites, meaning they infect beyond the skin and advance into the organ systems. Protozoa are single-celled endoparasites, while helminths, the worms, are multicellular endoparasites. This size difference is practical as well: protozoa require a microscope, whereas helminths can be enormous, with the fish tapeworm reaching over 30 feet.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Motility does not separate the groups; some protozoa are non-motile in parts of their life cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses the definitions; protozoa are the single-celled group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither group is prokaryotic, since parasites by the medical definition are eukaryotes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Infection limited to the skin surface describes ectoparasites, not either subcategory of endoparasite.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man has several days of diarrhea with blood and mucus after fecal-oral exposure on a farm. Stool microscopy shows a large single-celled organism whose entire outer edge appears fuzzy because it is covered with thousands of tiny hair-like projections. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balantidium coli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Giardia lamblia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plasmodium vivax

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trypanosome spp.

explanation.summary: Balantidium coli is the only ciliate known to infect humans and can cause gastroenteritis with diarrhea or dysentery.
explanation.whyCorrect: Parasites that move by cilia are rare causes of human disease, and B. coli is the only known ciliate that infects humans. Its fuzzy outer edge on microscopy is created by thousands of tiny cilia. B. coli is transmitted fecal-orally and usually causes asymptomatic infection, but in rare cases it produces gastroenteritis with accompanying diarrhea or dysentery.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Giardia lamblia is a flagellate with two nuclei and a few whip-like flagella, not a surface covered in cilia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Naegleria fowleri is an amoeba that moves by pseudopods and causes a brain infection rather than dysentery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasmodium vivax is a sporozoan transmitted by mosquitoes and causes malaria, not bloody diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trypanosome spp. are flagellates and are not identified in stool as large ciliated organisms.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with a severe frontal headache, fever, and vomiting that began 5 days after he spent an afternoon diving into a warm freshwater lake. Over the next day he develops a stiff neck and has a generalized seizure. A wet preparation of his cerebrospinal fluid shows motile amebae. Which of the following routes of entry best explains how this organism reached his brain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct extension from a middle ear infection through the mastoid air cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding of the meninges from an unrecognized lung infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingestion of lake water with absorption of the organism across the intestinal wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inoculation of the organism through a small abrasion on the skin of his leg

choices.label: E
choices.text: Penetration of the nasal mucosa with spread along the olfactory nerve

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri infects when contaminated water is forced up the nose, after which it invades the olfactory nerve and reaches the brain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infection begins when water containing the amoeba goes up the nose during diving, swimming, or nasal rinsing. The organism penetrates the nasal mucosa, infects the olfactory nerve, and travels along it into the brain, producing primary amebic meningoencephalitis. Finding motile amebae in the CSF of a patient with recent warm freshwater exposure is the classic picture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Spread from the middle ear is a route for bacterial meningitis, not for this free-living amoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Naegleria fowleri does not establish a pulmonary focus and does not seed the meninges through the bloodstream.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Swallowing water containing the amoeba does not cause illness; the organism must enter through the nose.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Naegleria fowleri is not acquired by inoculation through broken skin; skin ulcers after an outdoor exposure suggest a different parasite entirely.

questions.stem: Autopsy of a 19-year-old man who died of a rapidly progressive meningoencephalitis one week after water skiing shows amebic trophozoites tracking from the roof of the nasal cavity into the frontal lobes. Which of the following structures did the organism most likely traverse to enter the cranial cavity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cribriform plate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foramen ovale

choices.label: C
choices.text: Internal acoustic meatus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jugular foramen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superior orbital fissure

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri follows the olfactory nerve through the cribriform plate to reach the brain.
explanation.whyCorrect: The olfactory nerve filaments pass from the nasal roof into the anterior cranial fossa through the perforations of the cribriform plate. The amoeba uses this pathway to move from the nasal mucosa directly into the frontal lobes, which is why the disease is a meningoencephalitis rather than a simple meningitis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The foramen ovale transmits the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve and is not on the olfactory pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The internal acoustic meatus transmits the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves, far from the nasal roof.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The jugular foramen lies in the posterior cranial fossa and carries the internal jugular vein and lower cranial nerves.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The superior orbital fissure connects the orbit to the middle cranial fossa and does not communicate with the nasal roof.

questions.stem: A county health officer is drafting a public advisory about Naegleria fowleri. Which of the following exposures carries the greatest risk of infection in the United States?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drinking untreated well water on a rural farm in the fall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Showering in chlorinated municipal tap water in the winter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Swimming in a warm southern freshwater lake in August

choices.label: D
choices.text: Swimming in the ocean surf along the Gulf coast in July

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wading in a cold mountain stream during the early spring

explanation.summary: Cases cluster in warm freshwater in southern states during the summer months.
explanation.whyCorrect: Naegleria fowleri lives in warm bodies of fresh water such as lakes, rivers, and hot springs, and the majority of reported United States cases occur in southern coastal states during summer. A hot August day in a southern lake combines the warm water, the freshwater habitat, and the recreational diving that drives water up the nose.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Drinking water that contains the amoeba does not cause disease, so ingestion of well water is not the risk of concern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The amoeba is only rarely found in tap water, and properly chlorinated municipal water in winter is a very low-risk exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The organism is found in fresh water rather than in ocean surf.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism favors warm water; a cold stream in early spring is a poor habitat for it.

questions.stem: A family learns that the warm spring-fed pond behind their house has tested positive for Naegleria fowleri. Several family members have swallowed pond water while fishing, and none has been ill. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anyone who swallowed the water should be isolated from young children

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every household member should begin antiparasitic prophylaxis today

choices.label: C
choices.text: Household members should be managed as contacts of a reportable illness

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum antibody titers should be drawn now and repeated in two weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Swallowing water that contains the amoeba does not cause this infection

explanation.summary: Drinking water contaminated with Naegleria fowleri does not cause illness; only nasal entry does.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disease requires the amoeba to be forced up the nose so it can invade the olfactory nerve. Water that is swallowed passes through the gastrointestinal tract without causing infection, so the family needs advice about keeping water out of their noses rather than about ingestion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The infection is not transmitted between people, so isolation serves no purpose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no prophylactic regimen given after a possible environmental exposure to this organism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Person-to-person spread does not occur, so household members are not contacts in any meaningful sense.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serology is not how this infection is identified; diagnosis rests on visualizing the amoeba, PCR, or antigen detection in CSF or tissue.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman is admitted with fever, severe frontal headache, and vomiting. Her family reports that she soaked in a natural hot spring shortly before becoming ill, and primary amebic meningoencephalitis is suspected. Which of the following intervals between nasal exposure and the onset of symptoms is most typical for this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 to 7 days, with a median of about 5 days

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2 to 3 months, with a median of about 10 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: 2 to 4 weeks, with a median of about 3 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: 6 to 12 hours, with a median of about 8 hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: 12 to 36 hours, with a median of about 1 day

explanation.summary: Symptoms of primary amebic meningoencephalitis begin 1 to 7 days after nasal exposure, with a median of about 5 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: The incubation period is short but not immediate: symptoms typically begin within a week of the water exposure, with a median of roughly 5 days. Death usually follows 1 to 18 days after symptoms start, which is why the illness is so often recognized only at autopsy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A latent period of months is characteristic of other infections, not of this rapidly fatal amebic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A multi-week incubation period does not fit; most patients are ill within a week of exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An onset within hours is far too rapid for this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Onset on the first day after exposure is earlier than the typical 1 to 7 day window.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy with confirmed primary amebic meningoencephalitis has had a severe frontal headache, fever, nausea, and vomiting for 2 days. Which of the following new findings would indicate that his illness has progressed to the second stage of the disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A generalized seizure followed by altered mental status

choices.label: B
choices.text: A headache that becomes more severe when he lies flat in bed

choices.label: C
choices.text: A temperature that climbs above 39.5 C despite antipyretics

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nausea that returns whenever he attempts to eat solid food

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two further episodes of vomiting after he drinks clear fluids

explanation.summary: Stage 1 of PAM is headache, fever, nausea, and vomiting; stage 2 brings stiff neck, seizures, altered mental status, hallucinations, and coma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The CDC divides the illness into two stages. The first is nonspecific and mimics bacterial meningitis. The second is marked by neurologic deterioration: nuchal rigidity, seizures, confusion or altered mental status, hallucinations, and finally coma. A seizure with a change in mental status therefore marks the transition to stage 2.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Headache is a stage 1 feature; a change in its positional character does not define progression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fever is present from stage 1 onward, and a higher temperature alone does not mark progression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nausea is a stage 1 symptom and does not signal neurologic deterioration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vomiting belongs to stage 1 and its persistence does not indicate a new stage.

questions.stem: A water sample containing Naegleria fowleri trophozoites is transferred from nutrient-rich lake water into cold distilled water. Which of the following changes is most likely to be observed first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion of the trophozoites into non-feeding flagellated forms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fusion of the trophozoites into a large multinucleated syncytium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immediate conversion of the trophozoites into thick-walled cysts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of all motility with permanent attachment to the flask wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rapid replication of the trophozoites with increased feeding activity

explanation.summary: Adverse conditions first drive Naegleria fowleri from the ameboid trophozoite into a non-feeding flagellate form.
explanation.whyCorrect: The life cycle has three phases: ameboid trophozoite, flagellate, and cyst. When food is scarce or temperatures are extreme, the trophozoite converts into a non-feeding flagellate. Only if the adverse conditions persist does the organism go on to encyst. Despite using flagella in this stage, the organism is still called an amoeba.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This organism does not form a multinucleated syncytium at any point in its life cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Encystment is the later response, occurring only after adverse conditions persist beyond the flagellate stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The organism retains motility using either pseudopods or flagella depending on its form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nutrient-poor, cold conditions suppress feeding and replication rather than stimulating them.

questions.stem: The cold, nutrient-poor conditions in that same flask are maintained for several more weeks. Which of the following best describes the form the organism now predominantly takes and its significance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cyst form, which persists until the environment improves and is not contagious

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cyst form, which spreads between people by the respiratory droplet route

choices.label: C
choices.text: The flagellate form, which is the only stage able to survive in completely dry soil

choices.label: D
choices.text: The flagellate form, which is the stage transmitted directly from person to person

choices.label: E
choices.text: The trophozoite form, which is shed in stool and spreads by the fecal-oral route

explanation.summary: When adverse conditions persist, Naegleria fowleri encysts, and the cyst is a survival form that is not contagious.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cyst is the organism's response to prolonged adverse conditions and allows it to wait until the environment improves, at which point it reverts to the trophozoite. The cyst form is explicitly not contagious, consistent with the fact that this infection is never transmitted between people.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Respiratory droplet spread between people does not occur; infection requires water entering the nose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The flagellate is a transient, non-feeding swimming form, not a durable survival stage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no person-to-person transmission of this organism in any form.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The trophozoite is not shed in stool, and fecal-oral spread plays no role in this infection.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man is admitted with fever, headache, and confusion 4 days after swimming in a warm lake. Which of the following findings would confirm a diagnosis of Naegleria fowleri infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid-fast bacilli seen in a cytospin preparation of cerebrospinal fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Branching septate hyphae seen on a potassium hydroxide preparation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Budding yeast with a wide clear halo on an India ink preparation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gram-negative diplococci seen on a Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Motile trophozoites seen in a wet preparation of cerebrospinal fluid

explanation.summary: Naegleria fowleri is identified by seeing trophozoites or flagellates in CSF, biopsy, or tissue, or by PCR or antigen detection on those samples.
explanation.whyCorrect: The three standard approaches are direct detection of trophozoites and flagellates in CSF, biopsy, or tissue; detection of parasite nucleic acid by PCR on those same specimens; and detection of parasite antigen using specific antibodies in immunohistochemical testing. Seeing the motile amoeba in spinal fluid establishes the diagnosis at the bedside.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid-fast bacilli point to mycobacterial disease, not to a free-living amoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Septate hyphae on potassium hydroxide indicate a mold and would not be found in this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A wide clear halo on India ink indicates an encapsulated yeast, not an amoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gram-negative diplococci indicate bacterial meningitis, the illness this infection is most often confused with.

questions.stem: A hospital reviews a death from primary amebic meningoencephalitis that was recognized only at autopsy. More than three-quarters of these cases in the United States are diagnosed after death, and fewer than 5 of roughly 164 reported patients have survived. Which of the following best explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibody titers become detectable only several weeks into recovery

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lumbar puncture is contraindicated once meningeal signs have appeared

choices.label: C
choices.text: The illness is rare and progresses so fast that it is rarely considered

choices.label: D
choices.text: The organism cannot be visualized in cerebrospinal fluid during life

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism stays confined to brain tissue and never reaches the spinal fluid

explanation.summary: PAM is so rare and so rapidly progressive that it is seldom included in the differential diagnosis while the patient is alive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the early symptoms are indistinguishable from bacterial meningitis and the infection kills within 1 to 18 days of symptom onset, clinicians rarely consider it in time. Its rarity compounds the problem: with only about 164 reported cases since 1962 and roughly 98% mortality, it is almost never on the initial differential unless a history of swimming in warm, soil-contaminated water is elicited.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Diagnosis does not depend on antibody titers; direct detection, PCR, and antigen testing are used.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lumbar puncture is how the spinal fluid containing the amoeba is obtained; it is not the obstacle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trophozoites and flagellates can in fact be seen in cerebrospinal fluid from living patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism is recoverable from cerebrospinal fluid as well as from brain tissue.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation asks which household chores she should hand off to her husband. The couple keeps one indoor cat. Which of the following activities poses the greatest risk of Toxoplasma gondii infection for her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Brushing the cat's fur each evening after dinner

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emptying and scrubbing out the cat's litter box

choices.label: C
choices.text: Petting the cat while it sits on her lap at night

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refilling the cat's dry food and water bowls

choices.label: E
choices.text: Washing the cat's blanket in the household machine

explanation.summary: Toxoplasma gondii oocysts are shed in cat feces, so pregnant women should avoid contact with cat litter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cats release oocysts in their feces, and humans become infected by ingesting food or water contaminated with cat feces. Because the parasite can cross the placenta and infect the fetus, pregnant women are specifically advised to avoid contact with cat feces, which makes litter box duty the exposure to eliminate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Grooming a cat is not the described route of transmission; the parasite is acquired from feces or from meat.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Petting a cat does not transmit the parasite, which is why cat ownership itself need not be avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Handling food and water bowls does not involve contact with cat feces.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Laundering bedding is not a described route of infection for this parasite.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who has never owned a pet develops 2 weeks of low-grade fever, malaise, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Serology is positive for acute Toxoplasma gondii infection. He reports eating rare lamb and home-butchered venison several times a month. Which of the following best explains how he acquired the infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A bite from an infected female phlebotomine sandfly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contact with the saliva of an infected neighborhood cat

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingestion of tissue cysts present in undercooked meat

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhalation of aerosolized oocysts while cleaning out a barn

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmission during unprotected sexual contact with a partner

explanation.summary: Eating undercooked meat containing tissue cysts is a common route of Toxoplasma gondii infection, independent of cat ownership.
explanation.whyCorrect: Toxoplasma gondii infects a wide range of warm-blooded mammals, and the meat of infected animals contains tissue cysts. Consuming that meat undercooked delivers viable parasites to the gut, and this is one of the two common routes of human infection alongside ingestion of oocysts from cat feces. Healthy adults typically develop a mononucleosis-like illness, as here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sandfly bites transmit Leishmania species, not Toxoplasma gondii.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The parasite is acquired from cat feces, not from cat saliva or casual cat contact.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aerosol inhalation is not a described route of transmission for this parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sexual transmission characterizes Trichomonas vaginalis, not Toxoplasma gondii.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman has a 3-month history of abdominal discomfort, increasing fatigue, and intermittent diarrhea. Over the past year she has stopped eating red meat and now eats fresh fish several times a week, including sushi and ceviche. Serum vitamin B12 concentration is low. Stool examination shows large, oval eggs with an operculum at one pole. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia asiatica

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taenia solium

explanation.summary: Raw freshwater fish plus low vitamin B12 plus large oval operculated eggs in stool is diphyllobothriasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diphyllobothrium latum, the fish tapeworm, is acquired by eating raw or undercooked fish that contains the plerocercoid larva. Its eggs are oval with a small lid, the operculum, at one end and sometimes a slight knob at the other. A history of raw fish together with low B12 points to this infection, and finding these eggs in stool supports the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a free-living amoeba that causes rapidly fatal central nervous system disease, not an intestinal helminth that sheds eggs in stool.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Asian tapeworm is a pork-associated Taenia found only in Asia, and its eggs are the same round, striated Taenia eggs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The beef tapeworm is acquired from undercooked beef and sheds round eggs with a striated outer membrane, not operculated oval eggs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pork tapeworm is acquired from undercooked pork and also sheds round, striated eggs rather than operculated ones.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man has a 3-week history of moderate abdominal discomfort and infrequent diarrhea. He follows a fad "primal diet" and regularly eats raw beef. A tapeworm infection is suspected and stool microscopy is performed. Which of the following findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encysted larvae within fragments of striated muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oval eggs bearing an operculum at one pole

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proglottids with a rosette-shaped central uterus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Round eggs with striations around the outer membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Worm segments whose scolex bears two grooves

explanation.summary: All Taenia species shed round eggs with a striated outer membrane; raw beef points to T. saginata.
explanation.whyCorrect: Eating raw or undercooked beef transmits Taenia saginata. The eggs of every Taenia species are round and carry striations, or fine lines, all around the outer membrane, and small hooks can occasionally be seen inside the egg. These eggs confirm taeniasis but cannot identify the species.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cysticerci sit in the muscle of infected cattle and pigs; they are not a finding in a human stool specimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An operculated oval egg is the egg of Diphyllobothrium spp., which is acquired from raw fish rather than beef.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A rosette-shaped central uterus is the distinguishing feature of Diphyllobothrium proglottids, not Taenia proglottids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Two grooves, the bothria, are found on the Diphyllobothrium scolex, not on a beef tapeworm.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman has a first generalized seizure. She has no history of head trauma or prior neurologic disease. MRI of the brain shows multiple calcified lesions scattered through both cerebral hemispheres. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Seizures with multiple calcified brain lesions are the classic picture of neurocysticercosis from Taenia solium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Taenia solium is the only tapeworm in this brick whose eggs hatch after a human swallows them. The released larvae invade the intestinal wall, enter the bloodstream, and seed tissues including the brain, where they mature into cysticerci. The resulting inflammation leaves calcified lesions, and seizures are the most common presentation of neurocysticercosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm stays in the lumen of the small intestine and does not invade tissue or reach the brain.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This amoeba causes a fulminant meningitis; patients do not live long enough for calcified lesions to form.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Its eggs do not hatch when swallowed by humans, so it causes intestinal disease only and never tissue cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This filarial nematode causes lymphatic filariasis, not calcified intracranial lesions.

questions.stem: Humans are described as the definitive host for Taenia saginata, Taenia solium, and Taenia asiatica. Which of the following best describes what makes a host the definitive host for a parasite?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The parasite completes only larval development in it

choices.label: B
choices.text: The parasite forms tissue cysts in its skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: The parasite is delivered to it by an arthropod vector

choices.label: D
choices.text: The parasite lives in it without ever causing disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: The parasite reaches adulthood and sexual maturity in it

explanation.summary: The definitive host is where the parasite matures sexually and lays its eggs.
explanation.whyCorrect: A definitive host is the host in which the parasite reaches adulthood and sexual maturity and lays eggs. For all three Taenia species, humans fill that role: the swallowed cysticercus matures into an adult worm that attaches to the intestine with its scolex and sheds eggs and gravid proglottids in stool.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Supporting only larval development is exactly what defines the intermediate host, not the definitive host.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Forming cysticerci in muscle is what happens in the intermediate host, which for these tapeworms is cattle or pigs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taenia has no arthropod vector; it is acquired by eating undercooked meat containing cysticerci.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Whether infection causes symptoms is unrelated to host classification; most taeniasis is mild but humans remain definitive hosts.

questions.stem: A public health officer is mapping the global distribution of the three tapeworms that cause taeniasis. Which of the following statements about their geographic distribution is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All three species are evenly distributed worldwide

choices.label: B
choices.text: All three species are restricted to Asia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia asiatica is restricted to Asia, the others worldwide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia saginata is restricted to Asia, the others worldwide

choices.label: E
choices.text: Taenia solium is restricted to Asia, the others worldwide

explanation.summary: T. saginata and T. solium occur worldwide, while T. asiatica is found only in Asia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Taenia saginata and Taenia solium are found worldwide but are more prevalent in poorer countries where people live in close contact with pigs and cattle. Taenia asiatica, the Asian tapeworm, is found in Asia only.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Distribution is not even; the beef and pork tapeworms concentrate where people live closely with cattle and pigs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only Taenia asiatica is limited to Asia; the other two species occur on every continent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The beef tapeworm is worldwide in distribution, not confined to Asia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pork tapeworm is found worldwide; it is Taenia asiatica that is restricted to Asia.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man has intestinal infection with Taenia solium. His physician warns him that he faces a complication that patients with Taenia saginata do not face. Which of the following properties of Taenia solium accounts for this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Its adult worm grows far longer than that of T. saginata

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its eggs hatch when swallowed by a human and invade tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its eggs survive for years rather than months outdoors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its gravid proglottids hold more uterine branches per side

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its scolex anchors more deeply into the intestinal mucosa

explanation.summary: Only Taenia solium eggs hatch in humans, which is why only it causes cysticercosis and autoinfection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike T. saginata and T. asiatica, the eggs of T. solium hatch when consumed by humans and treat us the same way they treat pigs. The released oncospheres invade the intestinal wall, enter the blood, and form cysticerci in tissue. Because a patient who carries an adult worm can swallow his own eggs, this also produces autoinfection with repeated reinfection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adult T. solium worms are 2 to 7 m long, shorter than T. saginata, which is usually 5 m or less but may reach 25 m.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taenia eggs survive days to months in the environment, and egg durability does not confer tissue invasion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: T. solium proglottids carry 7 to 13 lateral branches per side, fewer than the 12 to 30 of T. saginata.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Both species attach with suckers on the scolex, and depth of attachment has nothing to do with tissue invasion.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman who has been a strict vegetarian since childhood has new-onset seizures, and MRI shows several cystic and calcified lesions in the brain. She lives with relatives who recently emigrated from a rural area where pigs roam freely. Which of the following best explains how she acquired this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She ate undercooked beef containing cysticerci from a cow

choices.label: B
choices.text: She ate undercooked pork containing cysticerci as a child

choices.label: C
choices.text: She drank lake water holding larvae shed by crustaceans

choices.label: D
choices.text: She swallowed tapeworm eggs shed by an infected household member

choices.label: E
choices.text: She was bitten by an insect that inoculated larvae in blood

explanation.summary: Cysticercosis follows swallowing T. solium eggs from human feces, not from eating meat.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tissue cysts come from swallowing T. solium eggs, which are shed in the stool of someone carrying an adult worm. Trace amounts of feces reach food and surfaces such as door handles and tables when handwashing is poor, so a person who has never eaten pork can still acquire cysticercosis from a household contact or food handler.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beef transmits T. saginata, whose eggs do not hatch in humans, so it cannot produce brain cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Swallowing cysticerci in meat produces an adult worm in the intestine, that is taeniasis, and she has never eaten pork.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Larval stages in crustaceans belong to the fish tapeworm, which never invades human tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Taenia has no arthropod vector; transmission is by eating cysticerci in meat or by the fecal-oral route.

questions.stem: A patient with taeniasis passes an intact adult worm. Examination of the head of the worm shows suckers together with a rostellum carrying two rows of hooks. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: A rostellum with two rows of hooks identifies the scolex of Taenia solium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the eggs of all Taenia species look alike, species identification depends on the passed proglottids or the adult worm. The scolex of T. solium carries four suckers plus a rostellum armed with two rows of hooks, which distinguishes it from the other tapeworms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm scolex has two grooves called bothria rather than suckers and hooks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a free-living amoeba, not a helminth, so it has no scolex at all.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The beef tapeworm scolex has four large suckers but no rostellum and no hooks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is a filarial nematode that causes lymphatic filariasis; it has no scolex.

questions.stem: An adult tapeworm recovered from a patient's stool has a scolex with four large suckers but no rostellum and no hooks. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Four large suckers with no rostellum and no hooks identify Taenia saginata.
explanation.whyCorrect: The scolex of T. saginata bears four large suckers and lacks both a rostellum and hooks. Since the eggs of all Taenia species are essentially identical, this feature of the recovered adult worm is what allows the beef tapeworm to be named.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm attaches with two grooves, the bothria, and has no suckers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is an amoeba rather than a worm, so it has no scolex.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pork tapeworm carries a rostellum with two rows of hooks in addition to its suckers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is a filarial nematode; it has no scolex and does not live in the intestinal lumen.

questions.stem: A gravid proglottid recovered from a patient's stool is examined. Approximately 20 lateral uterine branches are counted on each side of the central uterine stem. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Taenia saginata gravid proglottids have 12 to 30 lateral uterine branches per side.
explanation.whyCorrect: The number of uterine branches in a gravid proglottid separates the two main Taenia species. T. saginata has 12 to 30 lateral branches on each side of the proglottid, so a count near 20 fits the beef tapeworm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm proglottid has a rosette-shaped central uterus instead of counted lateral branches.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This is a single-celled amoeba and produces no proglottids of any kind.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pork tapeworm has only 7 to 13 lateral branches on each side of a gravid proglottid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This filarial nematode has no proglottids, so branch counting does not apply.

questions.stem: A gravid proglottid passed by a patient with taeniasis is examined and shows about 9 lateral uterine branches on each side. Which of the following is the most likely species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: Taenia solium gravid proglottids have only 7 to 13 lateral uterine branches per side.
explanation.whyCorrect: T. solium contains 7 to 13 lateral branches on each side of the gravid proglottid, a lower count than T. saginata. Identifying the species matters here because only T. solium can go on to cause cysticercosis and neurocysticercosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fish tapeworm proglottid shows a rosette-shaped central uterus, not branches to be counted.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This amoeba is not a worm and produces no proglottids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The beef tapeworm has 12 to 30 lateral branches per side, well above the count described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This filarial nematode has no proglottids and lives in lymphatics rather than the gut.

questions.stem: A patient passes a mass of worm segments. Microscopy shows that each segment contains a central uterus arranged so that it resembles a rosette of flower petals. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diphyllobothrium latum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Naegleria fowleri

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taenia saginata

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taenia solium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wuchereria bancrofti

explanation.summary: A rosette-shaped central uterus in the proglottid distinguishes Diphyllobothrium from Taenia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diphyllobothrium proglottids have central uteruses that look like flower petals, a rosette shape. This is the feature used to tell Diphyllobothrium spp. apart from Taenia spp. when segments are recovered from stool, since the eggs alone cannot separate Diphyllobothrium species from one another.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This free-living amoeba is not a segmented worm and forms no proglottids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Beef tapeworm gravid proglottids show 12 to 30 lateral uterine branches per side.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pork tapeworm gravid proglottids show 7 to 13 lateral uterine branches per side, not a rosette.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This nematode does not form proglottids; it causes lymphatic filariasis.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man returns from three months of agricultural work in rural Southeast Asia, where he often worked barefoot in wet fields. He first noticed an itchy rash on his feet, then developed a dry cough, and now has intermittent diarrhea and abdominal pain. Stool microscopy reveals motile rhabditiform larvae. Which of the following best describes how this organism entered his body?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct penetration of intact skin by filariform larvae in soil

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ingestion of embryonated eggs in contaminated drinking water

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingestion of undercooked freshwater fish containing larvae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ingestion of undercooked pork containing encysted larvae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhalation of aerosolized larvae from dried contaminated dust

explanation.summary: Strongyloides stercoralis is a soil-transmitted nematode whose filariform larvae burrow directly through intact skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Strongyloides spp., Ancylostoma spp., and Necator americanus are the soil-transmitted helminths: they are acquired when a person walks on soil contaminated with the parasite. Unlike the tapeworms acquired by eating undercooked meat, these roundworms do not have to be consumed at all — the filariform larval stage in soil burrows directly into the skin of the definitive host. Barefoot contact with warm, wet soil in a tropical region is the classic exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fecal-oral ingestion of embryonated eggs is the route for Ascaris spp., which cannot burrow through skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Undercooked freshwater fish transmits the fish tapeworm, not a skin-penetrating roundworm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ingestion of larvae encysted in undercooked meat describes the tapeworms, not a soil-transmitted nematode.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Helminths in this group are not transmitted by inhaled aerosols or respiratory droplets.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman who emigrated from a rural tropical region 12 years ago reports recurrent, intensely itchy linear red tracks over her buttocks and thighs; individual tracks appear and fade within hours. Stool examination reveals rhabditiform larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis. Which of the following terms best describes her rash?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cutaneous larva migrans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythema marginatum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Erythema migrans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Erythema nodosum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Larva currens

explanation.summary: The migrating, pruritic, linear rash caused by Strongyloides larvae burrowing through skin is called larva currens.
explanation.whyCorrect: When filariform larvae penetrate skin and wiggle through it searching for a blood vessel or lymphatic, they leave a mild, pruritic, erythematous, linear rash named larva currens. In chronic strongyloidiasis the same appearance recurs on the buttocks, perineum, and thighs because autoinfective filariform larvae burrow out of the perianal region and back into the skin there.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cutaneous larva migrans is the name given to the rash of Ancylostoma/Necator spp., not to the Strongyloides rash.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythema marginatum is a non-pruritic, evanescent ring-shaped rash unrelated to helminth migration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythema migrans is the expanding target-like rash of a tick-borne bacterial infection, not a larval track.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Erythema nodosum consists of tender subcutaneous nodules on the shins, not migrating linear tracks.

questions.stem: A patient becomes infected with Strongyloides stercoralis after walking barefoot on contaminated soil. Which of the following sequences best describes the infectious cycle of this parasite within the host?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ingestion of eggs, blood vessels, lungs, coughed up and swallowed, colon and cecum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ingestion of eggs, small intestine, colon, perianal skin, environment, reingestion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skin penetration, blood vessels or lymphatics, lungs, coughed up and swallowed, small intestine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skin penetration, lymph nodes, liver, portal circulation, small intestine, colon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skin penetration, subcutaneous tissue only, spontaneous death of larvae after weeks

explanation.summary: Strongyloides filariform larvae go skin to bloodstream or lymphatics to lungs, then are coughed up, swallowed, and mature in the small intestine.
explanation.whyCorrect: The filariform larva penetrates skin and burrows until it finds a blood vessel or lymphatic. It is carried to the lungs, where it matures further, then is coughed up and swallowed. Once in the small intestine the larva matures into an adult female, which embeds in the submucosa. This skin-blood-lung-gut route is shared with the hookworms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ingestion of eggs with a lung migration describes Ascaris spp., and those adults live in the small intestine, not the cecum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Egg ingestion followed by colonic maturation and perianal egg laying describes the pinworm cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no hepatic or portal phase in the Strongyloides cycle; larvae reach the lungs from the systemic circulation or lymphatics.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Larvae dying in the skin without reaching the circulation describes Ancylostoma braziliense, not S. stercoralis.

questions.stem: An adult Strongyloides stercoralis worm is recovered from the duodenal mucosa of an infected patient. Which of the following is most likely true of this worm and how it reproduces inside the host?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both male and female worms are present and reproduce sexually in the mucosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a female worm that produces fertilized eggs asexually in the submucosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a female worm whose eggs are fertilized by males arriving from the lungs

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a hermaphroditic worm that self-fertilizes within the intestinal lumen

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a male worm that fertilizes females embedded in the duodenal mucosa

explanation.summary: Only female Strongyloides adults parasitize humans, and they produce fertilized eggs asexually in the intestinal submucosa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Larvae that reach the small intestine mature into adult females; males do not cause infection. The female embeds in the submucosa of the small intestine and asexually produces fertilized eggs, which hatch in the mucosa to release rhabditiform larvae. Males and females do meet and reproduce sexually, but only outside the host, in the free-living soil cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both sexes mating in the intestine describes hookworms, which is precisely what distinguishes them from Strongyloides spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No male worms migrate from the lungs; the parasitic adult population in humans is female only.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick describes asexual production of fertilized eggs by the female, not hermaphroditic self-fertilization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Male Strongyloides worms do not establish infection in humans and are not found parasitizing the gut.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has had mild intermittent abdominal discomfort for 20 years. He immigrated from a tropical country two decades ago and has not traveled since. Stool studies now reveal Strongyloides stercoralis larvae. Which feature of this parasite best explains an infection persisting for 20 years without re-exposure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adult worms are continually reacquired from household contacts by fomites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adult worms survive in the small intestine for decades without laying eggs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eggs lie dormant in the biliary tree and hatch intermittently over decades

choices.label: D
choices.text: Encysted larvae in skeletal muscle periodically release progeny into the blood

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rhabditiform larvae mature to filariform larvae and reinvade gut or perianal skin

explanation.summary: Autoinfection lets Strongyloides complete its entire cycle inside one host, so infection is lifelong without treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rhabditiform larvae hatching in the intestinal mucosa do not have to leave the body. Some mature into filariform larvae that burrow back through the intestinal mucosa or through the perianal skin, find a blood vessel, and restart the lung-to-gut migration. This autoinfective loop means a person infected with Strongyloides spp. stays infected for life unless anti-parasitics are given.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Person-to-person fomite spread characterizes pinworm eggs, not Strongyloides filariform larvae.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Persistence depends on continuous reinfection of the host, not on unusually long-lived, non-reproducing adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Strongyloides eggs hatch in the intestinal mucosa; they do not lie dormant in the biliary tree.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Encystment in skeletal muscle is not part of the Strongyloides life cycle described in this brick.

questions.stem: Rhabditiform larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis are passed in the stool of an infected patient and reach warm, moist soil. In addition to developing into infective filariform larvae, which of the following can these larvae do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Develop into adults capable of reproducing only inside a canine host

choices.label: B
choices.text: Develop into male and female adults that reproduce within the soil

choices.label: C
choices.text: Embryonate over roughly 18 days before becoming able to infect skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Encyst within soil particles and remain infective for several decades

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enter a snail intermediate host before becoming able to infect humans

explanation.summary: Strongyloides has a free-living cycle in which soil-dwelling adults reproduce sexually outside any host.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rhabditiform larvae passed in the stool have two options. They can develop directly into filariform larvae that penetrate the next host's skin, or they can develop into male and female adults that reproduce sexually in the soil. That second option is the free-living cycle, in which adult worms can go on reproducing outside a host indefinitely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dogs can serve as definitive hosts, but free-living soil reproduction needs no host at all.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A required embryonation period in soil applies to Ascaris eggs, not to larvae that have already hatched.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Strongyloides larvae do not encyst in soil; they either develop to filariform larvae or become free-living adults.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No snail or other intermediate host is required for any stage of the Strongyloides life cycle.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man who immigrated from Southeast Asia is started on high-dose prednisone for a newly diagnosed autoimmune disease. Three weeks later he develops severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, hemoptysis, and gram-negative sepsis; chest radiograph shows diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Which of the following best explains his deterioration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A hypersensitivity reaction to dying worms triggered by the corticosteroid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acquisition of a new soil-transmitted infection while he was hospitalized

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct corticosteroid toxicity to gut mucosa allowing worms to invade

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of immune control over autoinfection causing hyperinfection syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactivation of larvae encysted in his skeletal muscle by the corticosteroid

explanation.summary: Severe immunosuppression, especially high-dose corticosteroids, converts chronic strongyloidiasis into hyperinfection syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: In chronic strongyloidiasis the immune system holds the autoinfective cycle in check. Severe immunosuppression or high-dose corticosteroid treatment lets the autoinfection cycle accelerate, and the parasite burden explodes. Burrowing larvae disseminate beyond the gastrointestinal tract and lungs, producing GI bleeding and obstruction, pneumonitis with hemoptysis and diffuse infiltrates, meningitis, and sepsis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The syndrome is driven by an enormous live parasite burden, not by an allergic response to dying worms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A newly acquired soil-transmitted infection could not produce disseminated disease within three weeks in a hospital.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Larvae penetrate intestinal mucosa as a normal part of autoinfection, independent of steroid mucosal toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Strongyloides does not encyst in skeletal muscle; the reservoir is the ongoing autoinfective cycle itself.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic strongyloidiasis develops hyperinfection syndrome with dissemination of larvae beyond the gastrointestinal tract and lungs. Even with appropriate anti-parasitic treatment, which of the following best approximates the mortality of this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Approximately 10 percent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Approximately 25 percent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Approximately 50 percent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Approximately 90 percent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Less than 1 percent

explanation.summary: Mortality of Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome with dissemination approaches 90 percent even when treated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although most Strongyloides infections are mild or asymptomatic, hyperinfection with dissemination is a catastrophic illness. Larvae spread throughout the body causing GI hemorrhage and obstruction, pneumonitis, meningitis, and sepsis. Mortality is near 90 percent even with treatment, which is why identifying and treating chronic infection before immunosuppression matters so much.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 10 percent figure would describe a serious but usually survivable illness, which this is not.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A one-in-four mortality is far lower than what disseminated strongyloidiasis carries.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This substantially understates the lethality of disseminated hyperinfection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Under 1 percent describes uncomplicated chronic strongyloidiasis, not hyperinfection with dissemination.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old asymptomatic woman from a strongyloidiasis-endemic region is evaluated before starting immunosuppressive therapy. Which of the following laboratory findings is present in roughly three-quarters of patients with chronic strongyloidiasis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated IgE or a mild eosinophilia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated serum IgA with thrombocytosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated serum IgM with lymphopenia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Microcytic anemia with a low ferritin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neutrophilia with a marked left shift

explanation.summary: Roughly 75 percent of patients with chronic strongyloidiasis have an elevated IgE or a mild eosinophilia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic strongyloidiasis is usually asymptomatic, so laboratory clues carry weight. About 75 percent of chronically infected patients show either an elevated IgE or mild eosinophilia, the expected type 2 immune signature of a persistent tissue-migrating helminth. These findings should prompt evaluation before starting corticosteroids or other immunosuppression.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Elevated IgA with thrombocytosis is not associated with this infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Elevated IgM with lymphopenia is not a described feature of chronic strongyloidiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microcytic anemia with low ferritin points to blood-feeding hookworms, not to Strongyloides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neutrophilia with a left shift suggests acute bacterial infection rather than a chronic helminth infection.

questions.stem: A clinician suspects chronic strongyloidiasis in a patient with years of intermittent diarrhea and a recurring migratory pruritic rash. Which of the following findings on specialized stool examination is the most common way this diagnosis is established?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mammillated eggs with rounded bumps over the outer shell

choices.label: B
choices.text: Motile rhabditiform larvae, or occasionally a passed adult

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proglottid segments containing branched uterine structures

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smooth-shelled eggs whose interior contains multiple nodules

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transparent elongated eggs that are flat along one side

explanation.summary: Strongyloidiasis is diagnosed by seeing rhabditiform larvae in stool, because the eggs hatch before they are passed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Specialized stool examination is the gold standard for strongyloidiasis. Because eggs hatch within the intestinal mucosa, what appears in stool is the rhabditiform larva, not an egg. Visualizing those larvae, or occasionally a passed adult, is the most common way the diagnosis is made. Parasite burden is low in chronic infection, so repeated samples are needed to approach full sensitivity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mammillated bumpy eggs are the unfertilized eggs of Ascaris spp.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Proglottid segments come from tapeworms, which are cestodes rather than nematodes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Smooth-shelled eggs with internal nodules are the eggs of Ancylostoma/Necator spp.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transparent elongated eggs flattened on one side are those of Enterobius vermicularis.

questions.stem: A patient with a high clinical suspicion for strongyloidiasis has had three separate specialized stool examinations, all negative for larvae. Which of the following is the best next step to increase diagnostic sensitivity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bronchoalveolar lavage, the preferred test in uncomplicated disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Colonoscopy, which reliably visualizes the adult worms in the gut

choices.label: C
choices.text: Duodenal aspiration, which samples the site where the adult worms reside

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral blood smear, which shows circulating filariform larvae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serologic testing, which is highly specific for Strongyloides spp.

explanation.summary: When stool studies are repeatedly negative, duodenal aspiration is the more sensitive, though more invasive, option.
explanation.whyCorrect: Parasite burden in chronic strongyloidiasis is low, so stool examinations are often falsely negative and must be repeated. Duodenal aspirates are more invasive than stool collection but have a higher sensitivity, sampling the site where the adult females are embedded and the larvae hatch. It is therefore the appropriate escalation after repeatedly negative stools.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bronchoalveolar lavage is invasive and reserved for hyperinfection when sputum is inadequate, not for uncomplicated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Strongyloides adults are only 1 to 6 mm long and are not sought by colonoscopy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Strongyloides larvae are not identified by examining a peripheral blood smear.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serology is available but cross-reacts with other parasitic species, so its usefulness is limited.

questions.stem: A critically ill patient with Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome has diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, but repeated sputum samples are inadequate for analysis. Which of the following procedures is most appropriate to recover the parasite from the lungs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bronchoalveolar lavage with instilled and aspirated saline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Open surgical lung biopsy with frozen-section examination

choices.label: C
choices.text: Percutaneous transthoracic needle aspiration of an infiltrate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat induced sputum after nebulized hypertonic saline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thoracentesis with microscopic examination of pleural fluid

explanation.summary: In hyperinfection, bronchoalveolar lavage can recover larvae from the lungs when sputum is inadequate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bronchoalveolar lavage is a minimally invasive procedure in which sterile saline is instilled into the lungs and aspirated back. Because hyperinfection sends larvae into the pulmonary tissue, sampling lung fluid this way can reveal the parasite. It is specifically useful when sputum does not provide a good sample, and because it is invasive it is reserved for exactly this situation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Open lung biopsy is far more invasive than needed when lavage can sample the same compartment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Needle aspiration of an infiltrate carries added risk and is not the described approach for recovering larvae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sputum sampling has already failed in this patient, which is the stated indication to move to lavage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The larvae disperse into lung tissue and airways, so pleural fluid is not the appropriate specimen.
